claims.text: The paper's internal self-citation pattern independently corroborates Puthoff's authorship despite the redacted cover: references 3, 16 and 19 are H. E. Puthoff papers, including "Polarizable-vacuum (PV) approach to general relativity", Found. Phys. 32, 927 (2002).

claims.nodeLabel: Advanced Space Propulsion Based on Vacuum (Spacetime Metric) Engineering
claims.text: The paper concludes that a metric-engineered craft would exhibit apparent superluminal motion, blueshifted emission, reduced effective mass permitting abrupt trajectory changes without internal stress, materials "hardened" so a craft "could, for example, impact water at high velocities without apparent deleterious effects", and sudden "cloaking" or "blinking out". These are the reported observables of UAP encounters restated as consequences of general relativity.

claims.nodeLabel: Advanced Space Propulsion Based on Vacuum (Spacetime Metric) Engineering
claims.text: Cover page reads: "29 March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1003-015", series "Acquisition Threat Support". The OCR renders the number as "DIA-08-i003-015".

Maccone co-authored with H. E. Puthoff and E. W. Davis, "Levi-Civita effect in the polarizable vacuum (PV) representation of general relativity", Gen. Relativ. Grav. 37, 483 (2005), which appears as reference 19 of Puthoff's own DIRD.
